questions.question: In a project selection model, each candidate project $j$ has a variable $y_j\in\{0,1\}$. What does $y_j=1$ mean?
options: Project $j$ is carried out in its first year only
Project $j$ fits within every year's budget
Project $j$ earns its return in one year only
Project $j$ is selected and carried out in full

questions.question: In the project selection model $\max\sum_jr_jy_j$ s.t. $\sum_ja_{tj}y_j\le B_t$ for every year $t$, $y_j\in\{0,1\}$ ($r_j$: return of project $j$, $a_{tj}$: its spending in year $t$, $B_t$: budget of year $t$), what does the left-hand side $\sum_ja_{tj}y_j$ of the year-$t$ constraint add up?
options: Year-$t$ spending of all candidate projects
Year-$t$ spending of the selected projects only
Spending of the selected projects over all years
Returns of the selected projects in year $t$

questions.question: In the project selection model $\max\sum_jr_jy_j$ s.t. $\sum_ja_{tj}y_j\le B_t$ for every year $t$, $y_j\in\{0,1\}$ ($r_j$: return of project $j$, $a_{tj}$: its spending in year $t$, $B_t$: budget of year $t$), what does $a_{23}$ denote?
options: The spending of project 3 in year 2
What project 2 spends during year 3
The return of project 3 in year 2
The year-2 budget left after project 3

questions.question: A project selection model uses $y_j\in\{0,1\}$ rather than $0\le y_j\le1$ for project $j$, whose full return is $r_j$. Which modelling statement does this reflect?
options: Each project is done fully or not at all, never part-funded
Each project may be part-funded and then earns that share of $r_j$
Each project's spending is the same in every year it runs
Each project is selected only if its return $r_j$ is positive

questions.question: In the project selection model $\max\sum_jr_jy_j$ s.t. $\sum_ja_{tj}y_j\le B_t$ for every year $t$, $y_j\in\{0,1\}$ ($r_j$: return of project $j$, $a_{tj}$: its spending in year $t$, $B_t$: budget of year $t$), why can the projects not be decided one at a time, independently of each other?
options: Each return $r_j$ depends on the other projects chosen
Each project must run in the same years as the others
Their spending draws on the same yearly budgets $B_t$
At most one project may be selected in each year $t$

questions.question: Four projects have returns $r=(8,7,4,10)$, year-1 spending $(6,1,7,6)$ with budget $B_1=11$, and year-2 spending $(6,7,5,7)$ with budget $B_2=13$; $y_j=1$ if project $j$ is selected and $0$ otherwise. Which selection satisfies both yearly budgets?
options: Projects 2 and 4
Projects 2 and 3
Projects 1 and 4
Projects 1 and 3

questions.question: Four projects have returns $r=(8,7,4,10)$, year-1 spending $(6,1,7,6)$ with budget $B_1=11$, and year-2 spending $(6,7,5,7)$ with budget $B_2=13$; $y_j=1$ if project $j$ is selected and $0$ otherwise. Which constraint is the year-2 budget?
A firm models five candidate projects with binary variables $y_1,\dots,y_5$. Before any budget constraint is imposed, how many selection vectors $y\in\{0,1\}^5$ are there?
With one capital budget of $10$, three projects cost $4$, $5$, $6$ and return $5$, $6$, $8$; each is selected in full or not at all. What is the largest total return?

Four projects have returns $r=(8,7,4,10)$, year-1 spending $(6,1,7,6)$ with budget $B_1=11$, and year-2 spending $(6,7,5,7)$ with budget $B_2=13$; $y_j=1$ if project $j$ is selected and $0$ otherwise. For the selection of projects 1 and 2, how much of the year-1 budget is left unused?

In the project selection model $\max\sum_jr_jy_j$ s.t. $\sum_ja_{tj}y_j\le B_t$ for every year $t$, $y_j\in\{0,1\}$ ($r_j$: return of project $j$, $a_{tj}$: its spending in year $t$, $B_t$: budget of year $t$), what happens if the yearly constraints are replaced by their single sum $\sum_t\sum_ja_{tj}y_j\le\sum_tB_t$?
options: Selections that were feasible may become infeasible
The same selections stay feasible, so nothing changes
Selections overspending in a year may become feasible
Each selection's total return $\sum_jr_jy_j$ changes

questions.question: In the project selection model $\max\sum_jr_jy_j$ s.t. $\sum_ja_{tj}y_j\le B_t$ for every year $t$, $y_j\in\{0,1\}$ ($r_j$: return of project $j$, $a_{tj}$: its spending in year $t$, $B_t$: budget of year $t$), which change makes the model choose as many projects as possible within the budgets?
options: Replace every budget $B_t$ by the number of projects
Replace every return $r_j$ by $1$ in the objective
Add the constraint $\sum_jy_j\ge1$ to the budgets
Change $\max\sum_jr_jy_j$ into $\min\sum_jr_jy_j$

questions.question: In the project selection model $\max\sum_jr_jy_j$ s.t. $\sum_ja_{tj}y_j\le B_t$ for every year $t$, $y_j\in\{0,1\}$ ($r_j$: return of project $j$, $a_{tj}$: its spending in year $t$, $B_t$: budget of year $t$), how is a project handled that spends money only in year 1 of a three-year plan?
options: Drop the year-2 and year-3 budget constraints
Give it its own variable $y_{tj}$ for each year $t$
Set $B_2=B_3=0$ for this project's budget rows
Set $a_{2j}=a_{3j}=0$ and keep one variable $y_j$

questions.question: Four projects have returns $r=(8,7,4,10)$, year-1 spending $(6,1,7,6)$ with budget $B_1=11$, and year-2 spending $(6,7,5,7)$ with budget $B_2=13$; $y_j=1$ if project $j$ is selected and $0$ otherwise. Which selection maximizes total return?
options: Projects 1 and 2, return 15
Projects 2 and 4, return 17
Projects 1 and 4, return 18
Project 4 alone, return 10

questions.question: Four projects have returns $r=(8,7,4,10)$, year-1 spending $(6,1,7,6)$ with budget $B_1=11$, and year-2 spending $(6,7,5,7)$ with budget $B_2=13$; $y_j=1$ if project $j$ is selected and $0$ otherwise. Allowing $0\le y_j\le1$, the best value is about $17.6$ at $y\approx(0.81,0.17,0,1)$. Which statement follows?
options: Rounding to projects 1 and 4 gives a plan returning $18$
Funding $81\%$ of project 1 is a valid plan worth $17.6$
No selection of whole projects can return more than $17.6$
The best selection of whole projects returns exactly $17$

questions.question: Four projects have returns $r=(8,7,4,10)$, year-1 spending $(6,1,7,6)$ with budget $B_1=11$, and year-2 spending $(6,7,5,7)$ with budget $B_2=13$; $y_j=1$ if project $j$ is selected and $0$ otherwise. Projects 1 and 2 are alternative designs, so $y_1+y_2\le1$ is added. Which selection is now optimal?
options: Projects 2 and 3, return 11
Project 4 alone, return 10
Projects 1 and 4, return 18
Projects 1 and 2, return 15

questions.question: In the project selection model $\max\sum_jr_jy_j$ s.t. $\sum_ja_{tj}y_j\le B_t$ for every year $t$, $y_j\in\{0,1\}$ ($r_j$: return of project $j$, $a_{tj}$: its spending in year $t$, $B_t$: budget of year $t$), which assumption lets the objective simply add $r_jy_j$ over the selected projects?
options: Returns do not depend on which other projects are chosen
Every project spends a positive amount in every year $t$
All yearly budgets $B_t$ are equal to one another
Every project's return $r_j$ exceeds its total spending

questions.question: In the project selection model $\max\sum_jr_jy_j$ s.t. $\sum_ja_{tj}y_j\le B_t$ for every year $t$, $y_j\in\{0,1\}$ ($r_j$: return of project $j$, $a_{tj}$: its spending in year $t$, $B_t$: budget of year $t$), with all $a_{tj}\ge0$: for a set of projects, what is the condition that each chosen project alone satisfies $a_{tj}\le B_t$ for every year $t$?
options: Enough for feasibility, but some feasible sets fail it
Equivalent to feasibility, as each chosen project is checked
Needed for feasibility, but some infeasible sets meet it too
Unrelated to feasibility, since only the yearly sums count

questions.question: Four projects have returns $r=(8,7,4,10)$, year-1 spending $(6,1,7,6)$ with budget $B_1=11$, and year-2 spending $(6,7,5,7)$ with budget $B_2=13$; $y_j=1$ if project $j$ is selected and $0$ otherwise. Project 4 has the highest return and fits both budgets alone. Why does adding projects in order of return fail here?
options: Project 4 must be in the optimum, but the order is wrong
Project 4 breaks the year-2 budget, so nothing can follow
Project 4 is optimal alone, as its return is the largest
Project 4 fits with no partner, so it ends at 10, not 15

questions.question: Four projects have returns $r=(8,7,4,10)$, year-1 spending $(6,1,7,6)$ with budget $B_1=11$, and year-2 spending $(6,7,5,7)$ with budget $B_2=13$; $y_j=1$ if project $j$ is selected and $0$ otherwise. The optimum, projects 1 and 2, leaves 4 of $B_1$ unused. If $B_1$ rises from 11 to 12, what is the new maximum return?
options: 15, since the year-1 budget was not binding
17, since projects 2 and 4 now fit both years
16, since one extra unit of budget adds about 1
18, since projects 1 and 4 now fit both years
